paper_title: ASyMOB Algebraic Symbolic Mathematical Operations Benchmark
caption: belowskip=0pt : Effect of equivalence-type perturbations. Note the substantial drop in success rate for most models, even when performance on the seed set is high.
model_annotation: The diagram displays the effect of equivalence-type perturbations on the success rates of various models. The horizontal axis lists model names, and the vertical axis represents the success rate as a percentage, ranging from 0% to 100%. For each model, there are five bars representing different equivalence types: "Seed", "'Equivalence-One-Easy'", "'Equivalence-One-Hard'", "'Equivalence-All-Easy'", and "'Equivalence-All-Hard'". Each bar is colored according to a legend provided in the top-right corner. The "Seed" bars are dark blue and consistently have the highest values, ranging approximately from 85% to 98%. The "'Equivalence-One-Easy'" bars are slightly lighter blue, with values ranging from about 70% to 90%. The "'Equivalence-One-Hard'" bars are even lighter, with values between roughly 30% and 60%. The "'Equivalence-All-Easy'" and "'Equivalence-All-Hard'" bars are light blue and very light blue, respectively, with values ranging from approximately 10% to 40% and 5% to 30%. The bars are not sorted in any particular order, and none are visually highlighted beyond their color coding. Overall, the diagram compares the success rates across models and equivalence types, showing a general trend of decreasing success rates as the equivalence type changes from "Seed" to "'Equivalence-All-Hard'".

model_annotations.English: This bar chart illustrates the success rates of various models under different equivalence-type perturbations. The horizontal axis lists the model names, each followed by "(Code)" or "(No Code)", indicating the presence or absence of code. The vertical axis represents the success rate as a percentage, ranging from 0 to 100, with a linear scale and labeled tick marks at regular intervals. Each model has five bars, representing 'Seed', 'Equivalence-One-Easy', 'Equivalence-One-Hard', 'Equivalence-All-Easy', and 'Equivalence-All-Hard', distinguished by different shades of blue. The 'Seed' bars for most models are above 80%, with the highest at approximately 96% for Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code) and Gemini 2.5 Flash (No Code). In contrast, the 'Equivalence-All-Hard' bars are significantly lower, with many below 20%, and the shortest at around 5% for Nemotron-Super-v1. The bars are not sorted in any specific order, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color differentiation.
